description: Fully responsive, interactive step-based geometry explorer for Grade 7 Mathematics — Line Segment Relationship Explorer. Canvas-based tool showing pairs of line segments in different configurations (perpendicular, angle meeting, converging, parallel) with animated progressive reveal. Includes MCQ practice mode with 5 questions and real-world examples with proper geometric illustrations. Uses Singularity Design System (Poppins font, #4A4DC9 primary, #FF7212 accent). Responsive across mobile (<480px), tablet (480–768px), and desktop (≥768px) via ResizeObserver.

width.description: Maximum component width in pixels. The component is fully fluid — it fills its container up to this max-width and auto-adapts all sizing via ResizeObserver breakpoints.

height.description: Reference height. Canvas height is computed responsively: ~65% of container width on mobile (capped 220px), ~50% on tablet (capped 280px), ~48% on desktop (capped 340px).

showModeSelector.description: Show/hide mode selector tabs. On mobile, tabs show icons only; on tablet+, icons with labels.

showNavigation.description: Show/hide prev/next buttons. On mobile, buttons show icon-only (chevrons); on tablet+, icon with text labels.

showPlayPause.description: Show/hide play/pause auto-advance button (hidden in practice mode)

showStepIndicator.description: Show/hide step counter pill in header. In practice mode, also shows score.

filterSteps.description: Array of step IDs to show (null = show all). Useful for focusing on specific concepts.

autoPlayDuration.description: Auto-advance delay in ms (0 = manual navigation only)

animationSpeed.description: Animation speed multiplier. Default animation duration is 1800ms / speed.

themeColor.description: Primary theme color (hex) — from Singularity Design System

darkMode.description: Enable dark mode (not yet implemented in canvas — reserved for future)

additionalProps.description: Tool-specific dynamic content passed by the agent

showGrid.description: Show background dot grid. Grid spacing auto-adapts: 30px on desktop, 20px when canvas < 300px wide.

gridSpacing.description: Base grid spacing in pixels (auto-reduces on small screens)

lineThickness.description: Default line thickness. Canvas auto-scales: uses 2.5 on mobile, 3.5 on desktop.

labelFontSize.description: Default label font size. Canvas auto-scales labels based on canvas width.

showProtractor.description: Show protractor tick overlay on angle steps (Step 3). Hidden when canvas < 300px.

segments.description: Custom line segments to display (coordinates are relative to canvas w/h)

realWorldExamples.description: Real-world examples shown in labels (Indian school context)

learn.description: Step-by-step exploration of line segment relationships: grid intro → perpendicular (90°) → angle meeting (115.3°) → converging → parallel → classify all four types

practice.description: 5-question MCQ quiz with geometric diagrams. Each question shows a line configuration on canvas and asks the student to identify the relationship or angle type. Immediate feedback with explanation. Final score shown after question 5.

real_world.description: Real-world perpendicular and parallel line examples with geometric illustrations — Indian classroom context (door frame, textbook, desk, railway tracks, notebook, ladder)

1.title: Exploring Line Segments
1.canvas: Empty dot grid with decorative fan lines and intro text. Mobile: shortened text.

2.title: Perpendicular Lines — 90°
2.canvas: Two full lines (l horizontal, m vertical) with arrowheads on both ends, intersection dot, 90° blue square symbol in top-right quadrant. Labels l and m in italic. Badge: 'Perpendicular — 90°'. Hint: 'Like a door frame corner'.

3.title: Meeting at an Angle — 115.3°
3.canvas: Two rays FG (210° from +x) and FH (94.7° from +x) emanating from point F. Red angle arc, protractor tick marks every 5° (major at 30°), degree numbers at major ticks. Badge: '115.3°'. Vocabulary box on wide screens (>450px). Labels F (endpoint), G, H.

4.title: Will They Meet? — Converging Lines
4.canvas: Segments PQ (upper-left) and RS (lower-right) as solid lines with endpoint dots. Dashed extensions from Q and S toward mathematically computed intersection point. Arrow heads converging. Pulsing red dot at intersection. Badge: 'They WILL meet if extended!' (shortened on mobile).

5.title: Never Meeting — Parallel Lines
5.canvas: Two horizontal lines l (primary) and m (accent) with arrowheads on all 4 ends. Dashed extensions. Direction ▸ markers. Three vertical dashed distance markers labeled d (italic). Badge: '∞ Never Meet — Parallel Lines ∞'. Hint: 'Like railway tracks'. Mobile: shortened labels.

6.title: Classify All Four Types
6.canvas: 2×2 grid with rounded cards. Top-left: Perpendicular with square symbol. Top-right: Angle meeting with arc. Bottom-left: Converging with dashed extensions to meeting point. Bottom-right: Parallel with direction markers. Mobile: abbreviated card labels (e.g. '⊥ 90°').

10.title: Question 1 of 5
10.question: What type of lines are shown here?

11.title: Question 2 of 5
11.question: If two line segments are extended and they meet, what are they called?

12.title: Question 3 of 5
12.question: What is the angle between two perpendicular lines?

14.title: Question 5 of 5
14.question: FG and FH meet at 115.3°. What type of angle?

20.title: Perpendicular in Daily Life
20.canvas: Three side-by-side illustrations: (1) Door frame — 3-sided rectangle with floor line, 90° symbols at all corners. (2) Textbook — full rectangle with ruled lines inside, margin line, 90° at corner. (3) Desk/Table — horizontal tabletop with vertical legs, floor line, 90° at all joints. Labels and badges for each. Summary line at bottom.

21.title: Parallel Lines Around Us
21.canvas: Three side-by-side illustrations: (1) Railway tracks — two vertical parallel rails with horizontal sleepers, 90° symbol, direction arrows, distance marker d. (2) Notebook — rectangle with 10 ruled parallel lines, margin line, direction arrows. (3) Ladder — two converging side rails with horizontal rungs, direction markers. Labels and badges for each. Summary line at bottom.

practiceMode.description: MCQ quiz with 5 questions. Each question renders a geometric diagram on canvas (static, not animated) and shows 4 multiple-choice options below. Immediate feedback on selection: correct answer highlights green (#22C55E), wrong answer shakes and highlights red (#EF4444) with explanation. Score tracked across all questions. Final score card shown after question 5 with gradient text.

diagramTypes.perpendicular: Two lines at 90° with arrowheads, square symbol, intersection dot
diagramTypes.parallel: Two horizontal lines with arrowheads and direction markers
diagramTypes.converging: Two segments with endpoint dots, dashed extensions meeting at a point
diagramTypes.obtuse_angle: Two rays from common point with 115.3° arc and badge

types.contained: Solid primary bg, white text (Next button)
types.outlined: White bg, primary border, primary text (Previous button)
types.highlight: Solid accent (#FF7212) bg, white text (Play/Pause button)

canvasColors.accentLine: #FF7212 (perpendicular vertical, parallel line 2, angle ray 2, ladder rungs)

responsive.strategy: ResizeObserver on container element measures actual rendered width. Three breakpoints derive all sizing.

mobile.badges: Shortened text (e.g. 'Will meet!' instead of 'They WILL meet if extended!')

canvasRendering.dpr: Uses window.devicePixelRatio for crisp rendering on Retina/HiDPI
canvasRendering.width: containerWidth - responsivePadding, set via canvas.width (resolution) and canvas.style.width: '100%' (display)
canvasRendering.labelFonts: Scale by canvas width: w<300 → small, w<500 → medium, else full size

touchTargets.minimum: 44×44px on all interactive elements (Apple HIG standard)

teachingNotes.step1: Blank canvas with grid. Introduce that we will explore line segment relationships.
teachingNotes.step2: Reveal perpendicular lines with 90° blue square symbol. Ask what is special about this angle. Real-world: door frame, textbook edge.
teachingNotes.step3: Show FG and FH meeting at 115.3°. Introduce protractor reading and vocabulary (endpoint, degree measure, obtuse angle). Vocabulary box appears on wider screens.
teachingNotes.step4: Two segments heading towards each other that will meet if extended. Ask student to predict WHERE. Intersection computed mathematically via parametric line-line intersection.
teachingNotes.step5: Two segments going same direction. Ask if they would EVER meet. Previews parallel lines. Equal-distance markers prove constant separation.
teachingNotes.step6: All four types in a 2×2 grid. Ask student to classify them. Labels adapt for mobile.
teachingNotes.practice: 5 MCQ questions with immediate feedback. Diagrams rendered statically on canvas. Score tracked across all questions. Explanations teach even when wrong.
teachingNotes.step20: Three real-world perpendicular examples: door frame, textbook, desk. Each with proper geometric lines and 90° symbols on canvas.
teachingNotes.step21: Three real-world parallel examples: railway tracks (with perpendicular sleepers), ruled notebook (with perpendicular margin), ladder (with rungs). Each with proper geometric lines on canvas.

instructionsForStudent: Watch as different pairs of line segments appear. For each pair, think about: Do they meet? If so, at what angle? If they do not meet, would they meet if extended? Use the vocabulary words — endpoint, midpoint, intersect, perpendicular, degree measure — to describe what you see.

Student asks: Show me all types of line relationships
